observations.why: Ratification language performs the settling of the async job contract; the declarative act records a decision already made, not a position being argued for.
Operational guarantee stated as a settled rule of the ratified contract — 'no' functioning as an absolute constraint the speaker expects to hold, not a claim still open to evidence.
The speaker explicitly labels this as a decision and states the dispatch-then-poll pattern as the settled operational design, not a proposal being weighed.

mints.name: LabelledDecisionAsSettled
mints.title: naming the act of settling as a 'key decision' the group acts on
mints.frame: Does the speaker mark the moment of commitment by naming it a decision, rather than by arguing for the position?
